transcript: The show here at the fringe to make me have cry the most is easily Steve Burns alive. As somebody who was a slightly older than the target demographic but had younger siblings, I watched a lot of Blues Clues, but this one person show that Steve Burns has crafted chronically his time on this show dealing with all of the pervasive rumors that he had passed away. There is a vulnerability to the show that is refreshing to see. And not only that, but Steve Burns is an incredible storyteller and absolutely sucks you in. Steve Burns Alive is not only an incredible look at internet culture, but also parasocial relationships and both for the positive and the negative. Because I think a lot of times we have a power in the anonymity of being able to say whatever on the internet and feeling like it doesn't have consequences. And Steve Burns is absolutely the proof that what you say in the comment sections does have consequences. Well, I found a lot of it to be immensely relatable, but also a fascinating look at such a vibrant piece of our pop culture history. Blues Clues was such a huge moment in the late 90s, early 2. And so to hear the story from Steve's side of things was fascinating and highly entertaining and really eye opening. I'm so glad that Steve Burns is sharing his story here at the fringe. I highly recommend catching this if you can it. Is currently playing at Underbelly Cowgate, through the rest of the fringe.
